Accusé par Mélétos, Anytos et Lycon, Soc: Accused by Meletus, Anytus and Lycon, Socrates was found guilty by 280 votes to 221. He first proposed, provocatively, to be fed at public expense in the Prytaneum, like a benefactor.
Diogène et son père auraient été chassés: Diogenes and his father were said to have been driven from Sinope for debasing the currency. When Alexander asked what he wanted, he told him to stand out of his sun; when Plato defined man as a "featherless biped", he brought him a plucked cock.
Les Premiers Analytiques datent d'enviro: The Prior Analytics date from around 350 BC. Aristotle's logic dominated for more than two thousand years: Kant still judged it "completed" in 1800, before Boole (1854) and then Frege (1879) went beyond it.
Né à Cordoue en 1126, Averroès est juge: Born in Córdoba in 1126, Averroes was a judge and physician at the Almohad court. In 1195, his books were burned and he was exiled to Lucena. Dante placed him in Limbo, and Raphael painted him in The School of Athens.
L'idée est bien plus ancienne qu'Ockham: The idea is much older than Ockham: Aristotle, Ptolemy and Robert Grosseteste already preferred the simplest explanation. The phrase "entities must not be multiplied without necessity" comes from John Punch in 1639, and Libert Froidmont claimed to have coined "Occam's razor" in 1649.
Ses frères l'enlèvent et le gardent pris: His brothers kidnapped him and held him prisoner for nearly a year to stop him joining the Dominicans. His fellow students called him "the dumb ox". In December 1273, after a mystical experience, he stopped writing: it all seemed "like straw" to him. He was canonised in 1323.
Le mythe naît au XIXe siècle : Washingto: The myth was born in the 19th century: Washington Irving published a romanticised biography of Christopher Columbus in 1828, mistaken for a scholarly work, and Antoine Letronne wrongly attributed a flat Earth to the Church Fathers in 1834.
Machiavel l'écrit en 1513, quelques mois: Machiavelli wrote it in 1513, a few months after being arrested, tortured and banished by the returning Medici, and yet dedicated it to Lorenzo de' Medici. The book came out after his death, in 1532, and the Church placed it on the Index in 1559.
Élevé en latin comme langue maternelle,: Raised with Latin as his first language, Montaigne withdrew in 1571, at 38, to the tower of his château, which he dedicated by an inscription to "his freedom, tranquility and leisure". He was nonetheless mayor of Bordeaux from 1581 to 1585.
Érasme l'écrit en 1509 chez son ami Thom: Erasmus wrote it in 1509 at his friend Thomas More's house in London. The Latin title, Moriae Encomium, is a pun: it can also be read "In Praise of More". Hans Holbein the Younger illustrated a copy.
Écrite en latin, Utopia paraît en 1516 e: Written in Latin, Utopia came out in 1516 and was only translated into English in 1551. More also played on eu-topos, "the good place". On his island, property is held in common and people work about six hours a day.
Né à Tunis en 1332, Ibn Khaldoun écrit l: Born in Tunis in 1332, Ibn Khaldun wrote the Muqaddimah over more than three years, sheltered by a Berber tribe. He met the conqueror Timur outside Damascus. Historian Arnold Toynbee called it "the greatest work of its kind".
Le débat part d'une question laissée ouv: The debate began with a question Porphyry left open in the 3rd century: do genera and species exist in things or only in the mind? Boethius passed it on to the Middle Ages by translating his Isagoge; Roscelin answered that universals are mere vocal sounds.
Bruno est détenu sept ans à Rome ; le ca: Bruno was held for seven years in Rome; Cardinal Bellarmine demanded that he recant, in vain. To his judges he reportedly said: "Perhaps you pronounce this sentence against me with greater fear than I receive it." His statue was unveiled at the site of the pyre on 9 June 1889.
L'édition de 1580 ne compte que deux liv: The 1580 edition had only two books; that of 1588 added the third. Montaigne then annotated a copy by hand, the "Bordeaux Copy", kept at the city's municipal library.
Saint Augustin avait déjà répondu aux sc: Saint Augustine had already answered the sceptics, in the early 5th century in The City of God: "If I am mistaken, I exist." Avicenna also proposed the "floating man" thought experiment, about self-awareness without any perception.
Pierre de Fermat découvre la même idée d: Pierre de Fermat discovered the same idea independently, without publishing it, and Nicole Oresme was already using similar constructions in the 14th century. The two perpendicular axes only took hold after La Géométrie was translated into Latin in 1649.
Les Pensées sont un recueil, publié aprè: The Pensées are a collection, published after his death, of notes Pascal had never published: that is where the wager first appears in writing.
Le 27 juillet 1656, la communauté juive: On 27 July 1656, Amsterdam's Jewish community issued against Spinoza, aged 23, the harshest ban in its history, never lifted. He lived by grinding lenses and died in The Hague in 1677, aged 44; his friends then published his works.
L'image est ancienne : Aristote compare: The image is old: Aristotle already compared the mind to a tablet with nothing written on it. In the 12th century, Ibn Tufail's novel Hayy ibn Yaqdhan follows a child who learns everything alone on an island; its 1671 Latin translation influenced Locke.
Sextus Empiricus soulevait déjà la diffi: Sextus Empiricus already raised the difficulty in antiquity. Hume formulated it in 1739 in his Treatise of Human Nature, then in 1748: for him, it is habit, not reason, that makes us expect tomorrow.
Evelyn Beatrice Hall écrit cette phrase: Evelyn Beatrice Hall wrote the sentence in The Friends of Voltaire, in the chapter on Helvétius, to illustrate Voltaire's attitude. It is still often attributed to him.
Kant ne quitte guère Königsberg que pour: Kant hardly left Königsberg except to tutor in nearby towns, from 1748 to 1754. After long years of silence, he published the Critique of Pure Reason in 1781, at about 57.
La formule vient du poète latin Horace,: The phrase comes from the Latin poet Horace, around 20 BC, in a letter to Lollius: "He who has begun is half done; dare to know; begin!" Melanchthon quoted it in 1518 in Wittenberg, and Foucault took up Kant's text in 1984.
Le livre est interdit en France, mis à l: The book was banned in France, put on the Index and burned in Geneva; Rousseau had to flee to avoid prison. Voltaire, who criticised it, protested: to burn a book of argument is to admit you lack the wit to answer it.
Le projet devait au départ traduire la C: The project was first meant to translate Englishman Ephraim Chambers's Cyclopaedia (1728). Suspended in 1752, then stripped of its privilege in 1759, the work went on in secret. The Chevalier de Jaucourt alone wrote about a quarter of the articles.
En 1699, Nicolas Fatio de Duillier accus: In 1699, Nicolas Fatio de Duillier accused Leibniz of plagiarising Newton. The 1713 Royal Society report that sided with Newton was written by Newton himself. Yet it is Leibniz's notation, dy/dx, that prevailed.
Popper oppose les théories qui font des: Popper contrasted theories making risky predictions with psychoanalysis and Marxism, whose followers explained away any fact after the event. His example: no list of white swans proves they all are, but a single black swan refutes the idea.
Kuhn prend pour exemple le passage de l': Kuhn's example is the shift from Ptolemy's astronomy to Copernicus's, in 1543. Kant had already spoken in 1787 of a "revolution in the way of thinking".
En 1885, sa sœur Elisabeth épouse Bernha: In 1885, his sister Elisabeth married Bernhard Förster, a nationalist and antisemite; Nietzsche did not attend the wedding. They founded the colony of Nueva Germania in Paraguay. Later she compiled The Will to Power, and Hitler attended her funeral in 1935. Recent work, however, questions the idea of deliberate falsification.
Le Deuxième Sexe se serait vendu à envir: The Second Sex reportedly sold about 22,000 copies in its first week. The Vatican put it on the Index, where it remained until the Index was abolished in 1966. The first English translation, in 1953, cut whole passages.
Eichmann est enlevé en Argentine par des: Eichmann was seized in Argentina by Israeli agents in 1960, tried in 1961 and executed in 1962. Arendt covered the trial for The New Yorker, where her report appeared in five articles. The book sparked fierce controversy, notably with Gershom Scholem.
Russell trouve le paradoxe en mai 1901 e: Russell found the paradox in May 1901 while looking for a flaw in a proof by Cantor. Frege replied on 22 June 1902 and added an appendix to his book: nothing worse can befall a scientific writer than to see one of the foundations of his edifice shaken. Zermelo had found it around 1899, without publishing it.
Sartre avait écrit le 14 octobre 1964 à: Sartre had written to the Nobel Institute on 14 October 1964 asking to be removed from the list. A prisoner of war in 1940, he had written his first play in a camp in Trier. On 19 April 1980, 50,000 Parisians followed his coffin.
Sartre prononce cette conférence le 29 o: Sartre gave this lecture on 29 October 1945 at the Club Maintenant in Paris, before a packed hall. The text came out in 1946, and Sartre later regretted publishing it.
Camus commence l'essai en 1940, pendant: Camus began the essay in 1940, during the fall of France. He starts from what he calls the only philosophical question that matters: must one kill oneself after recognising life's absurdity? His answer is no.
Wittgenstein prend ses notes comme solda: Wittgenstein took his notes as a soldier in the First World War and finished the book on leave in summer 1918. The 1922 English edition had an introduction by Bertrand Russell. At the time he thought he had solved all of philosophy's problems.
Élu au Collège de France fin 1969 à une: Elected to the Collège de France in late 1969 to a chair in the "history of systems of thought", Foucault co-founded the Prison Information Group in February 1971. He died of AIDS on 25 June 1984; his partner Daniel Defert then founded the AIDES charity.
Le livre paraît chez l'éditeur Julius Sp: The book was published by Julius Springer with the date 1935 printed on it. Popper himself rewrote it in English: The Logic of Scientific Discovery came out in 1959.
Philippa Foot imagine son tramway en réf: Philippa Foot devised her trolley while thinking about debates on abortion and the doctrine of double effect. A version already existed in 1905 in a questionnaire by Frank Chapman Sharp, and it was Judith Jarvis Thomson who named it the "trolley problem" in 1976.
Bentham meurt le 6 juin 1832. Selon son: Bentham died on 6 June 1832. Following his will, his body was dissected and then preserved by Thomas Southwood Smith, dressed in his clothes; his real head, judged too macabre, was replaced with a wax one. In 2020, he was placed at the entrance of UCL's new Student Centre.
Dans le même livre de 1785, Kant donne u: In the same 1785 book, Kant gave another formula: treat humanity, in yourself and in others, always also as an end and never merely as a means.
L'éthique des vertus revient au premier: Virtue ethics came back to the fore with Elizabeth Anscombe's article "Modern Moral Philosophy" in 1958, then with Alasdair MacIntyre's After Virtue in 1981. The four cardinal virtues are already in Plato's Republic.
L'idée est plus ancienne qu'Aristote : «: The idea is older than Aristotle: "Nothing in excess" was carved on the front of the temple at Delphi. It is also found in China in Confucius's way of the mean, and in the Buddha's "Middle Way".
Singer écrit cet essai en 1971 face à la: Singer wrote this essay in 1971 in response to the starvation of refugees during the Bangladesh Liberation War. William MacAskill came across it in a seminar and later helped found the effective altruism movement.
Richard Ryder lance le mot dans une broc: Richard Ryder launched the word in a privately printed pamphlet in Oxford in 1970, protesting against animal experimentation. He wrote: "Since Darwin, scientists have agreed that there is no 'magical' essential difference between humans and other animals."
Une forme négative de la règle figure dé: A negative form of the rule already appears on an Egyptian papyrus from the Late Period (664-323 BC): "That which you hate to be done to you, do not do to another." It is also found in Hillel the Elder, in the Talmud, and in the Mahabharata.
Le premier raisonnement connu de ce type: The first known reasoning of this kind is in the Summa Theologica, on self-defence: Thomas Aquinas allows that one may kill an attacker if one aims to defend oneself, not to kill.
En 2010, Felipe De Brigard renverse l'ex: In 2010, Felipe De Brigard turned the experiment around: of students told they were already plugged in, 54% wanted to disconnect, but only 13% if told their real life was that of a maximum-security prisoner. He saw it mostly as status quo bias.
Le site est lancé en 2016 par l'équipe d: The site was launched in 2016 by Iyad Rahwan's team at the MIT Media Lab. The results outline three broad cultural clusters: for example, East Asian countries spare the young less often than others.
Hobbes écrit le Léviathan pendant la gue: Hobbes wrote Leviathan during the English Civil War. Historian Hugh Trevor-Roper summed it up: "The axiom, fear; the method, logic; the conclusion, despotism."
Montesquieu publie le livre anonymement: Montesquieu published the book anonymously in Geneva, after about ten years of work; the Church put it on the Index in 1751. He describes the English system at length, and the work inspired the framers of the US Constitution.
L'économiste William Vickrey avait décri: Economist William Vickrey had described the same thought experiment as early as 1945, and John Harsanyi formalised it in 1955, but to defend utilitarianism. Rawls coined the phrases "original position" and "veil of ignorance".
Pour écrire Les Politiques, Aristote fai: To write the Politics, Aristotle had 158 constitutions of Greek cities collected to compare their strengths and weaknesses. The text may come partly from students' notes taken at the Lyceum.
En 1831, Tocqueville part avec Gustave d: In 1831, Tocqueville left with Gustave de Beaumont to study American prisons for the French government. They stayed about nine months and used the trip to observe the whole of society. The book came out in two parts, in 1835 and 1840.
Mill conçoit l'essai en 1854 avec sa fem: Mill conceived the essay in 1854 with his wife Harriet Taylor, and they rewrote it together. She died suddenly in 1858; Mill published it the following year without changing it, to "consecrate it to her memory", calling it their joint production.
Marx écrit ces notes à Bruxelles en 1845: Marx wrote these notes in Brussels in 1845 and did not publish them. Engels edited them and published them in 1888; the original text only appeared in 1924.
Montaigne affirmait que son ami l'avait: Montaigne claimed his friend wrote it at 16 or 18, but the text more likely dates from 1552-1553, when La Boétie was 22. It circulated in copies and was only printed in 1576, after his death; the Huguenots took it up.
Popper le formule dans une note de La So: Popper set it out in a note to The Open Society and Its Enemies: "Unlimited tolerance must lead to the disappearance of tolerance." He linked it to a "paradox of freedom" noted by Plato. Rawls, in 1971, called for tolerating the intolerant except when the free society's survival is at stake.
Platon tente l'expérience en vrai : en 3: Plato tried it for real: in 367 BC, his disciple Dion invited him to Syracuse to advise the young tyrant Dionysius II. The pupil resisted, and nothing came of it. Later, the emperor Marcus Aurelius was seen as a philosopher king.
Weber donne cette conférence le 28 janvi: Weber gave this lecture on 28 January 1919 in Munich, to a students' association, in the midst of the German Revolution. An extended version came out in July 1919.
Thoreau refuse de payer l'impôt pour pro: Thoreau refused to pay the tax to protest against slavery and the war with Mexico. He made it into a lecture in 1848, then the essay Resistance to Civil Government in 1849.
C'est la princesse Élisabeth de Bohême q: It was Princess Elisabeth of Bohemia who raised the awkward question, in a letter of 20 June 1643: how can an unextended soul move a body? Their correspondence lasted until Descartes's death in 1650.
Galien la décrit le premier au IIe siècl: Galen first described it in the 2nd century, naming it konarion, "little cone". Descartes made it the "principal seat of the soul" in The Passions of the Soul (1649). Its hormone, melatonin, was only isolated in 1958 by Aaron Lerner at Yale.
Leibniz imaginait déjà un cerveau agrand: Leibniz already imagined a brain enlarged to the size of a mill, where one would only see parts pushing each other. In 1961, a short story by Soviet writer Anatoly Dneprov had a whole stadium of people, who knew no Portuguese, simulate a translation program.
Turing prédisait qu'autour de l'an 2000,: Turing predicted that around the year 2000, an average interrogator would have no more than a 70% chance of identifying the machine after five minutes. In 1966, the ELIZA program, which mimicked a psychotherapist, already fooled some users.
L'article de Thomas Nagel paraît en octo: Thomas Nagel's article appeared in October 1974 in The Philosophical Review. Daniel Dennett noted that in 1950, B. A. Farrell had already raised a similar question in the journal Mind.
Chalmers lance l'expression en 1994, dan: Chalmers launched the phrase in 1994, in a talk at the consciousness conference in Tucson, Arizona, before his 1995 article. Leibniz and Thomas Huxley had put forward similar arguments.
Charles Sanders Peirce introduit le mot: Charles Sanders Peirce introduced the word quale in 1866, and C. I. Lewis used it in its modern sense in 1929. The "inverted spectrum" question comes from John Locke, in 1689.
En 1925, C. D. Broad imaginait déjà un a: In 1925, C. D. Broad already imagined an archangel who knew everything about the structure of ammonia yet could not predict its smell. Jackson eventually changed his mind: in 2023 he said he no longer accepts his own argument.
Hans Kornhuber et Lüder Deecke avaient d: Hans Kornhuber and Lüder Deecke had discovered this "readiness potential" in 1965. Libet also noted that the movement could still be cancelled: he spoke of "free won't". In 2012, Aaron Schurger and colleagues saw it rather as spontaneous fluctuations in neural activity.
Selon Plutarque, les Athéniens gardèrent: According to Plutarch, the Athenians kept the ship until the time of Demetrius of Phalerum. In the 17th century, Thomas Hobbes made the puzzle harder: what if a second ship were rebuilt from the old planks taken out?
Hilary Putnam en propose la première ver: Hilary Putnam proposed the first version in the 1960s, comparing the mind to a Turing machine. By the mid-1970s he himself began to question it, and Ned Block countered in 1980 with a "brain" made of the whole population of China.
Le scénario vient de Gilbert Harman en 1: The scenario comes from Gilbert Harman in 1973. Putnam took it up in 1981 to argue that the sentence "I am a brain in a vat" refutes itself. Zhuangzi's butterfly dream already raises a similar question.
Russell racontait l'histoire d'un poulet: Russell told the story of a chicken fed every day by the man who, one fine morning, wrings its neck. Hume had posed the problem in 1739; in 1955, Nelson Goodman invented a variant with the predicate "grue".
Le manifeste du cercle paraît en 1929. M: The circle's manifesto appeared in 1929. Moritz Schlick was murdered in 1936 by a former student, and Nazi Germany's annexation of Austria in 1938 ended the circle in Vienna.
Pierre Duhem limitait cette idée à la ph: Pierre Duhem limited this idea to physics. Quine extended it to all knowledge, including logic and mathematics, in "Two Dogmas of Empiricism", before partly backing down on logic.
Le livre devait être un débat avec Imre: The book was meant to be a debate with Imre Lakatos, who would defend scientific reason while Feyerabend attacked it; Lakatos died suddenly in 1974. Feyerabend explained that "anything goes" is not his principle, but the terrified exclamation of a rationalist who takes a closer look at history.
Les médecins hippocratiques voulaient dé: Hippocratic physicians already wanted to distinguish their reasoning from mythical accounts. In 1983, Larry Laudan judged that philosophy had failed to draw this line and proposed speaking instead of reliable or unreliable knowledge.
Né Imre Lipsitz en Hongrie en 1922, Laka: Born Imre Lipsitz in Hungary in 1922, Lakatos changed his name to escape the Nazis, spent three years in prison under the communist regime, then fled in 1956. A professor at the London School of Economics, he died suddenly in 1974. His motto: philosophy of science without history of science is empty.
Galilée avait déjà vu Neptune fin 1612 e: Galileo had already seen Neptune in late 1612 and early 1613, but took it for a star. Galle received Le Verrier's letter on the morning of 23 September 1846 and found the planet that very night, with Heinrich d'Arrest. Englishman John Couch Adams had made a similar calculation, hence a priority dispute.
Cette idée est surtout associée à Hanson: This idea is mainly associated with Hanson, Kuhn and Feyerabend, in the late 1950s and early 1960s. Pierre Duhem had probably already put it forward, at least implicitly, some fifty years earlier.
L'article s'intitule « Transgresser les: The article was titled "Transgressing the Boundaries: Towards a Transformative Hermeneutics of Quantum Gravity" and appeared in a special issue on the "Science Wars". Sokal revealed the hoax about three weeks later in the magazine Lingua Franca. In 2018, the "grievance studies" affair replayed it.
Les projets Many Labs du Center for Open: The Many Labs projects of the Center for Open Science followed: 186 researchers from 60 labs re-tested 28 psychology findings, and half failed to replicate, despite large samples.
Le nom latin experimentum crucis est ens: The Latin name experimentum crucis was later coined by Robert Hooke, and Newton used it in the Opticks for the prism experiment showing that white light is made of different rays.
